consumer: The frontend's threat-indicator caller asking 'has any monster noticed/detected the avatar?', which an engine-computed monster-awareness predicate answers (e.g. monster::sees(avatar) / aggro/tracking-destination state), not raw position.
scope: Per-monster engine awareness/detection state toward the avatar across the relevant monsters, not merely whether a monster sits inside the render window.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities (monsters window) — it iterates g->all_monsters(), filters by in_export_window, and writes index/type/pos/hp/hallucination but emits NO awareness/detection/aggro field, so the 'noticed' sub-goal is unanswerable from this surface.
divergence: A monster standing inside the export window but unaware of the avatar (asleep/idle, has not seen it) vs one that has detected and is tracking the avatar: the raw-state dump reports both identically (same pos/hp), so 'has any monster noticed the avatar' is silently wrong.
